clue.text: Former problem reported with porridge

indicators.note: reported means the word for a problem is heard spoken, giving a word of the same sound

parts.note: a sum is an arithmetic problem
porridge is British slang for a prison sentence, doing time

explanation.surface: Someone recalls an old difficulty, mentioned over a bowl of breakfast oats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Porridge' is British slang for time served in prison, not oats here.
explanation.definitionFit: Sometime as an adjective means one-time or erstwhile, as in a sometime professor.

clue.text: Catch separate bridge players turning over

indicators.note: turning over tells us to read the combined letters from right to left

parts.note: to part is to separate
North and East are two of the four seats at a bridge table

explanation.surface: Someone tries to catch out a bridge pair by splitting them as they play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning over' flips PARTNE, giving the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To entrap someone is to snare or catch them, often by trickery.

clue.text: We personally use lovers badly

indicators.note: badly signals that the letters of the two words are jumbled into a poor order

explanation.surface: A confession that we treat our partners poorly.
explanation.definitionFit: The reflexive pronoun for 'we' stresses that we did something in person, ourselves.

clue.text: Victoria — a queen and head of church

parts.note: Vic is a short form of the name Victoria
R stands for Regina, queen

explanation.surface: Queen Victoria is presented as head of the Church of England.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests the monarch heading the national church; actually it is a parish priest.
explanation.definitionFit: A vicar is the priest in charge of a Church of England parish, its head.

clue.text: A sign of rank cheese, one left unfinished

indicators.note: left unfinished means both words lose their final letter

parts.note: chevre is French goat's cheese
taken as written

explanation.surface: Some ranking emblem is somehow a cheese with a piece left uneaten.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left unfinished' cuts the last E from CHEVRE and from ONE.
explanation.definitionFit: A chevron is the V-shaped stripe on a sleeve showing military rank.

clue.text: Gleeman arranged a varied selection

indicators.note: arranged signals that the letters are put into a fresh order, like music arranged

explanation.surface: A medieval minstrel put together a medley of songs.
explanation.walkthrough: A gleeman is a medieval minstrel, which makes 'arranged' read musically.
explanation.definitionFit: A melange is a mixture or medley of assorted things.

clue.text: Contract arrived with Royal Academy for picture provider

parts.note: a compact is an agreement or contract
came means arrived
RA is the abbreviation for the Royal Academy of Arts

explanation.surface: An agreement with the art academy to supply paintings.
explanation.walkthrough: The Royal Academy steers toward paintings; the provider is a small camera.
explanation.definitionFit: A small point-and-shoot camera is a device that provides photographs, or pictures.

clue.text: Beer girl might put specially for chap who's cheating?

indicators.note: put specially means the letters are set out in a special new order

explanation.surface: A barmaid might arrange things to dupe a man who is deceiving.
explanation.walkthrough: A thimblerigger runs the shell game, hiding a pea under one of three thimbles.
explanation.definitionFit: A thimblerigger is a swindler running the three-thimble trick, so a man who cheats.

clue.text: Plant blooming fragrantly on the house I had in South Africa

parts.note: something on the house is given free

indicators.note: had in means the abbreviation for the country holds the next letter within it

explanation.surface: A sweet-smelling flower was given free at a house I lived in, in South Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: The freesia is indeed native to South Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: Freesias are scented flowering plants of the iris family, prized for their perfume.

clue.text: Adult to plead guilty after regular letters from girl?

indicators.note: after places the confession phrase behind the letters from the girl
regular letters from means take every other letter, the first and third

parts.note: to own up is to confess or plead guilty

explanation.surface: A grown woman admits her guilt following a letter from a young girl.
explanation.definitionFit: A grown-up is a fully mature person, an adult.

clue.text: Drab colour of old terminal

parts.note: the live terminal is the electrically charged one, as in a plug

explanation.surface: A dull paint shade from an old airport building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terminal' suggests an airport or the end; here it is the live terminal in wiring.
explanation.definitionFit: Olive green is a dull, drab greenish-brown colour.

clue.text: What might make uneasy UN fairly relaxed?

parts.note: if the letters spelling easy go away from the word uneasy, just UN remains

explanation.surface: Asks what would calm a nervous United Nations.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as an instruction: let EASY leave 'uneasy' and only UN is left.
explanation.definitionFit: Easy-going describes a calm, tolerant, unworried temperament, so fairly laid-back.

clue.text: Offer old useless item that fan's abandoned

indicators.note: abandoned means the word for an admirer is left out

parts.note: a fandangle is an old word for a useless ornament or trinket
a fan is an admirer; the 's stands for 'has' before the indicator

explanation.surface: Someone tries to sell off an old gadget an enthusiast no longer wants.
explanation.definitionFit: To dangle something, like a carrot, is to hold it out as a tempting offer.

clue.text: A hire fee follows computer programme patent

indicators.note: follows puts the article and the fee behind the software term

parts.note: an app is an application, a computer program
rent is the fee for hiring something

explanation.surface: Licensing software for a charge after it has been patented.
explanation.walkthrough: 'patent' looks like a noun, a legal right; here it is the adjective meaning obvious.
explanation.definitionFit: Patent as an adjective means plain or obvious, a synonym of evident.

clue.text: Candle holder about to get inserted into cake

indicators.note: to get inserted into means one piece is placed within the cake word

parts.note: a scone is a small plain cake
C is short for circa, about

explanation.surface: A birthday candle being pushed into a cake.
explanation.definitionFit: A sconce is a wall bracket holding candles or lights.

clue.text: Join forces, working finally in pool

indicators.note: in puts the final letter of working within the word for a pool

parts.note: a mere is a small lake or pool

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of the word working

explanation.surface: Swimmers team up, finally working together in the pool.
explanation.definitionFit: To merge is to combine or amalgamate, as companies uniting.

clue.text: Algebraic proof has them almost more confused

indicators.note: confused tells us to jumble the combined letters
almost means the word more is not complete, losing a letter

explanation.surface: A maths proof leaves students even more bewildered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' here drops the first letter of 'more', leaving ORE to mix with THEM.
explanation.definitionFit: A theorem is a proposition proved by logical steps, as in algebra.

clue.text: Mean measure of second French wine resulted in great anger

parts.note: a mo is a moment, a second
vin is the French word for wine
to give can mean to produce or result in
rage is great anger

explanation.surface: A stingy measure of French wine made someone furious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mean' suggests stinginess; it is the statistical average.
explanation.definitionFit: A moving average is a statistical mean recalculated over a sliding window of data.

clue.text: Story is not any volume by Fitzgerald?

parts.note: no means not any
Ella is the first name of jazz singer Ella Fitzgerald

explanation.surface: A tale that is not one of F. Scott Fitzgerald's books.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests the novelist F. Scott Fitzgerald; here it is the singer Ella.
explanation.definitionFit: A novella is a short novel, a prose story.

clue.text: Tale teller gets Conservative inside to desert Europe

indicators.note: inside means the party abbreviation goes within the word for deserting

parts.note: to rat is to desert or betray

explanation.surface: A storyteller reports a Tory joining up to abandon the EU.
explanation.definitionFit: A raconteur is a skilled teller of anecdotes, a storyteller.

clue.text: Cheese one's left hosts served in bowl

indicators.note: served in means the shortened hosts are placed inside the bowl

parts.note: a pan is a bowl-shaped vessel

indicators.note: left means the single letter has departed from the word for hosts

parts.note: a host is an army, so hosts are armies
one is the numeral I; the 's stands for 'has' before left

explanation.surface: A cheese that one person left out is served by hosts in a dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hosts' looks like party givers; here it means armies.
explanation.definitionFit: Parmesan is a hard Italian cheese, grated over pasta.

clue.text: An odd situation has arisen with one of your setter's drinks?

parts.note: one of the setter's drinks is some unspecified thing
your setter is I, the setter speaking; the 's is 'is' here
to sup is to drink

explanation.surface: Something strange is going on with the setter's drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as a statement by the setter: some thing I sup, one of the setter's drinks.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom says something unusual or suspicious is happening.

clue.text: Standard clubs must have interior redesigned

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for clubs in card games

indicators.note: redesigned means the word interior has its letters laid out afresh

explanation.surface: Golf clubs need their interiors refitted to meet a standard.
explanation.definitionFit: A criterion is a standard by which something is judged.

clue.text: Town with people working on ring road

parts.note: staff are the people working somewhere
O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: A town where workers are busy building a ring road.
explanation.walkthrough: STAFFORD is the county town of Staffordshire in the English Midlands.
explanation.definitionFit: Stafford is an English town, the county town of Staffordshire.

clue.text: Book half-finished by excellent biographer

indicators.note: half-finished means only the first half of the word book is used

parts.note: swell is a dated word for excellent

explanation.surface: An excellent biographer leaves a book half-written.
explanation.walkthrough: James Boswell wrote the famous Life of Samuel Johnson.
explanation.definitionFit: James Boswell is celebrated as the biographer of Samuel Johnson.

clue.text: State of Washington perhaps reduced current area

indicators.note: reduced means the first president's first name loses its last letter

parts.note: George is the first name of George Washington, an example
I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: Washington State, perhaps, has a reduced flow in some area.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State of Washington' suggests the US state; 'State' is the definition and Washington is George.
explanation.definitionFit: Georgia is one of the United States, and also a country in the Caucasus.

clue.text: Be furious about fit for plug

indicators.note: about means the angry word surrounds the word for a fit

parts.note: to spit is to be furious
a go is a bout or fit, as in a go of illness

explanation.surface: Someone is enraged about whether a plug fits.
explanation.definitionFit: A spigot is a peg or plug for stopping the vent of a cask.

clue.text: Wound up when deprived of large racket

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the letters are read from bottom to top
when deprived of means the letter for large is taken away

parts.note: a lesion is a wound

explanation.surface: Someone gets wound up and loses a large tennis racket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wound up' reads as agitated; 'Wound' is a noun, LESION, and 'up' reverses ESION.
explanation.definitionFit: A racket is a loud din, and noise is its everyday synonym.
